feedback.answered: A1 formation: dispatchLogs assigns current-term indices, stores logs, and only after StoreLogs succeeds reports the local match and wakes replicators. replicateTo and pipelineDecode accept successful replies after checking for a response term newer than the request; updateLastAppended reports the last request entry to the replication state's commitment object. commitment counts only configured voters, takes the majority order statistic and advances monotonically only at or beyond this leader's startIndex. leaderLoop consumes its notification, updates committed configuration and gathers committed inflight logs. processLogs sends command/barrier tuples to the asynchronous FSM worker; its lastApplied update means dispatch progress, whereas applySingle completes the future after FSM.Apply returns. A2 authority: follower timeout checks local voter eligibility; a candidate uses a campaign-local reply channel, electSelf increments and persists term through setCurrentTerm and requests one vote per configured voter, and requestVote checks membership, known leader, term, prior vote and log freshness before persisting a grant. A new leader allocates a fresh commitment object and dispatches a no-op. On loss of leadership it closes replication stop channels and fails pending log and verification futures; replication objects retain their own commitment references, so the observed accounting path is not an unconditional write into a subsequent leader's fresh commitment. Configuration admission waits for the previous configuration and a current-term entry to be committed, then changes the accounting voter set. Followers reject older AppendEntries terms and mismatched predecessor terms, replace conflicting suffixes, roll latest configuration back when truncation crosses it, and dispatch up to the received commit bound. The FSM interface independently states that Apply is called after majority commitment. These are observed mechanisms and interface requirements, not proof of their composition.
remaining: Core readiness remains incomplete: read replication-state construction/removal, leader lease/verification, snapshot installation and startup recovery, configuration validation, persistence setters and remaining FSM/client completion paths before recording a usable core_overview.

Investigate whether a legal catch-up history can retain a divergent local suffix beyond the prefix matched by one limited request when the leader commit index already extends past that request. Dedicated heartbeat requests have LeaderCommitIndex zero and do not supply this trigger; predecessor matching and conflict truncation are contrary protections. Establish a same-history producer path rather than injecting arbitrary entries.

connection.explanation: Support is eligible within the captured leader tenure and current voter set. feedback.answered: For ordinary append catch-up with accurate persisted-log metadata and a normal matching-prefix/divergent-suffix history, the sender does not first send an arbitrary early matching batch. A new tenure starts nextIndex at the leader end plus one. Rejection backs up one position, or jumps to a shorter follower end plus one. For a retained divergence at d, predecessor checks reject until predecessor d-1; the next request starts at d and truncates the conflicting suffix before applying the commit bound. A shorter follower has no suffix beyond the end hint. Successful ordinary replication catches up through its target before enabling the pipeline, which starts at the last successful nextIndex. Dedicated heartbeats carry no commit index. Thus the apparent receiver-only gap does not establish a defect under the selected normal sender history. This is a sourced conditional explanation, not an executed negative result or proof of all commit paths.

items.rationale: Reviewed the fixed plan and assurance_generated_test.go for artifact 0b43318d5be04e4c8baa57ddea29a7a6 and raw execution 7f8208006dcd48b98fddb2bea55e61df. The accepted claim explicitly forbids counting Nonvoter acknowledgements toward the voter threshold; the test checks that local clause, not the entire public API consequence. Its oracle compares measured v.votes with initial self vote plus a successful selected peer only if that peer is a Voter in the fixed configuration. This is independent of the implementation tally and uses a <= comparison, allowing pending/under-counted support rather than requiring success. BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, electSelf, peer processRPC/requestVote, verifyLeader, heartbeat, actual InmemTransport AppendEntries, peer appendEntries, notifyAll and vote execute. Three same-term grants establish the election prerequisite. The driver substitutes campaign state-transition scheduling and worker construction using the read startStopReplication fields; it does not forge responses or change suffrage. Delaying other workers through the short observation is a permitted asynchronous schedule. verifyLeader reads latest voter count, worker maps and operation fields, not commitIndex or no-op completion. runLeader normally dispatches a no-op before entering leaderLoop, but that dispatch does not establish any additional eligibility guard consumed by this selected entry; omission limits whole-loop reachability, not this local counting observation. The bootstrapped membership is fixed throughout; no claim that its configuration entry was committed is needed by this entry. The wrapper closes its stop channel after the real RPC and before returning to heartbeat, which still executes notifyAll; joining the worker observes that processing independently of threshold success. Each fixture has a unique operation label shared by admission and result; no expected tally or mutable term is used to filter correlation. Both parsed operations matched their own admission and produced complete result events with no parser errors. Raw voter control: final_votes=2, eligible_votes=2, success=true, same_future=true, threshold_notified=true. Raw nonvoter witness: final_votes=2, eligible_votes=1 with the same successful transport/completion diagnostics and threshold notification. The monitor preserves that violating event rather than failing the Go test or filtering it away. These observations answer whether nonvoter support is counted and can reach the threshold, not whether a stale client read or successful public Future occurred. Considered alternatives and boundaries: The voter-filtered leader lease can later step down a leader without quorum; it is not checked by verifyLeader/vote when they count this acknowledgement. Actual public Future completion is absent: the driver consumes the threshold notification without running leaderLoop completion. This prevents attributing a public API success or stale read to this witness. All voters granted the earlier election. Those grants establish prior authority but are not fresh acknowledgements for the later verification; only the selected worker ran after registration.

feedback.answered: A1 formation: dispatchLogs assigns current-term indices, stores logs, and only after StoreLogs succeeds reports the local match and wakes replicators. replicateTo and pipelineDecode accept successful replies after checking for a response term newer than the request; updateLastAppended reports the last request entry to the replication state's commitment object. commitment counts only configured voters, takes the majority order statistic and advances monotonically only at or beyond this leader's startIndex. leaderLoop consumes its notification, updates committed configuration and gathers committed inflight logs. processLogs sends command/barrier tuples to the asynchronous FSM worker; its lastApplied update means dispatch progress, whereas applySingle completes the future after FSM.Apply returns. A2 authority: follower timeout checks local voter eligibility; a candidate uses a campaign-local reply channel, electSelf increments and persists term through setCurrentTerm and requests one vote per configured voter, and requestVote checks membership, known leader, term, prior vote and log freshness before persisting a grant. A new leader allocates a fresh commitment object and dispatches a no-op. On loss of leadership it closes replication stop channels and fails pending log and verification futures; replication objects retain their own commitment references, so the observed accounting path is not an unconditional write into a subsequent leader's fresh commitment. Configuration admission waits for the previous configuration and a current-term entry to be committed, then changes the accounting voter set. Followers reject older AppendEntries terms and mismatched predecessor terms, replace conflicting suffixes, roll latest configuration back when truncation crosses it, and dispatch up to the received commit bound. The FSM interface independently states that Apply is called after majority commitment. These are observed mechanisms and interface requirements, not proof of their composition.

formation.explanation: Leader stores indexed current-term logs and reports its own match; per-peer replication verifies successful responses and accounts last sent entries or installed snapshot. Current voter majority and tenure startIndex select commit advancement. Leader propagates commit through append requests; followers check term and predecessor, reconcile entries, select a local bound and dispatch through processLogs. FSM execution is asynchronous; client success follows actual Apply completion.

context.explanation: Follower timeouts and transfer trigger campaigns over latest voters. Pre-vote checks plausibility without persisting term; actual election increments durable term, persists votes and uses log freshness. Campaign replies are private to the attempt. Leader entry creates fresh commitment and workers; higher-term RPC/reply, lease loss or self-removal ends authority, stops old workers and fails pending futures. Install/startup recover log/snapshot and configuration context; transfer catches target up before TimeoutNow.

connection.explanation: Support is eligible within the captured leader tenure and current voter set. Fresh tenure accounting and a current-term no-op prevent simply reusing old majority indexes; old workers retain old commitment/stepDown channels. Persisted history constrains votes, while a new leader reconciles follower suffixes before local consumption. Configuration changes are admitted one at a time after current-term commitment and immediately reinterpret voter support. Already dispatched FSM work is distinct from remaining inflight futures, so leadership loss cannot imply rollback. Snapshot recovery reinstates applied prefix/configuration and can supply catch-up support.
